docs.bookmarks.add: <kbd>Ctrl+D</kbd> saves the current search as a bookmark, and <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+B</kbd> organizes them.
docs.bookmarks.history: Recent searches are not recorded while Privacy Mode is on or search history is switched off.
docs.bookmarks.recall: Type : followed by a bookmark's name to run it.
docs.bookmarks.sidebar: View → Sidebar shows a column with your bookmarks, the quick filters, your drives and your recent searches. Drag bookmarks to reorder them; click a drive to search only that drive.
docs.bookmarks.title: Bookmarks and the sidebar
docs.cli.completions: freally completions prints completions for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell, including modifier names and your bookmarks.
docs.cli.formats: --json, --ndjson and --csv print results for scripts, -0 prints NUL-separated paths for xargs -0, and --fields chooses the columns. The exit code says whether anything matched.
docs.cli.intro: The freally command searches the same index as the app, through the same indexer, in the same query language.
docs.cli.manage: freally index shows the indexer's status and can pause, resume, verify, compact or rebuild it; freally bookmark saves, lists and deletes bookmarks.
docs.cli.strict: --strict-everything refuses any query that uses something Everything does not have, and names it — the way to check that a query works in both.
docs.cli.title: The command line
docs.drives.lists: File → Export Results… (Ctrl+S) saves the results as Everything's .efu file list, CSV, plain text, an M3U playlist of the audio files, or NDJSON for a script. File → Open File List… (Ctrl+O) searches inside a list, Everything's included, instead of the index, until you choose Close File List.
docs.drives.title: Unplugged drives and file lists
docs.drives.unplugged: When you unplug a drive, everything indexed on it stays searchable. Its results carry a badge with the drive's name, so they also answer which drive a file is on, and volume: searches one drive by its name. A drive that comes back on another letter or mount point is still recognised.
docs.faq.missing.indexing: The first index may still be running: the status bar says so.
docs.faq.missing.permissions: Its folder may be unreadable: open Permission Health….
docs.faq.missing.roots: Its folder may not be indexed: check the folders, drives and exclusions under Settings → Indexes.
docs.faq.missing.title: Why is a file missing from the results?
docs.faq.rebuild.body: Tools → Index maintenance → Force Rebuild Index… clears the index and builds it again from the start. Verify Index… and Compact Index… in the same menu check it and make it smaller.
docs.faq.rebuild.title: How do I start the index again?
docs.faq.smaller.body: Exclude folders full of files you never look for, such as node_modules and .git, under Settings → Indexes → Exclude.
docs.faq.smaller.title: How do I make the index smaller?
docs.faq.title: Questions
docs.filters.p1: Quick filters limit results to a kind of file in one click: Audio, Compressed, Document, Executable, Folder, Image and Video. Each one carries every extension Everything's own filter does, and more — 65 audio types, 79 video, 77 image, 86 document and 70 archive.
docs.filters.p2: You can also type them, with the aliases you would guess: audio:, video:, image:, document:, executable: and archive:, or music:, photos:, docs: and zip:.
docs.filters.p3: Source code is not filed under Document, unlike in Everything; ext:c;cpp;h brings that set back. To keep a search of your own as a filter, choose Search → Add to Filters…, and edit them with Organize Filters… (Ctrl+Shift+O).
docs.filters.title: Quick filters
docs.health.index: Tools → Index maintenance → Index Health… shows, for each place being watched, whether changes arrive live or only when it is rescanned, how far behind the index is, and how many changes were dropped. When something is wrong it says what, with a one-click rebuild where that is the fix.
docs.health.permissions: A folder the app cannot read looks exactly like an empty one. Permission Health…, in the same menu or from the "folders skipped" badge in the status bar, lists the folders that were skipped, the system's reason, and the fix. On macOS it checks whether Full Disk Access is granted and opens the right settings page if not.
docs.health.title: Index Health and skipped folders
docs.intro: How to use Freally Sourcerer as it is built today, on the road to 1.0; the guide grows with every version. On macOS, read Ctrl as Cmd: the menus show your system's own keys.
docs.language.p1: Sourcerer speaks eighteen languages. Choose one in Settings → Locale and the whole app — menus, settings, dialogs and the status bar — switches at once, without a restart. Arabic lays the window out right to left.
docs.language.title: Languages
docs.lenses.audio: Audio: what an audio file measures — loudness in LUFS, silence, dynamic range, length, codec and sample rate — worked out the first time a search asks, and kept until the file changes.
docs.lenses.content: Content: the text inside PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, plain text and Markdown, source code in 32 languages, JSON, CSV and YAML, mail, and zip, 7z and tar archives, without unpacking them. Not yet connected to the search bar.
docs.lenses.filename: File name: names and paths, with wildcards, regular expressions and Everything's modifiers. The fastest of the five.
docs.lenses.intro: Sourcerer has five lenses, all reading the same index. Today the file-name, audio and property lenses answer your searches; the content and similarity lenses are built but not yet connected to the search bar — that comes on the road to 1.0.
docs.lenses.prefix: Lenses can be switched on and off in View → Lenses.
docs.lenses.properties: Properties: what a file's own header says — seventy-two properties across images, camera data, video, documents, programs, installers, shortcuts, archives, fonts, mail and SQLite databases.
docs.lenses.similar: Similarity: names close to what you typed, for when you remember a file only roughly. Not yet connected to the search bar; until it is, a search that finds nothing offers the closest real name instead.
docs.lenses.title: The five lenses
docs.portable.mac: On macOS, the Data folder is made beside the app, not inside it, because writing inside an app breaks its signature.
docs.portable.p1: To run Sourcerer from a USB stick, put an empty file named portable.flag beside the app, or start it with --portable. The index, settings, bookmarks and logs then live in a Data folder beside the app, and nothing is registered with the computer: no background service, no link handler and no updater. Update a portable copy by replacing its folder.
docs.portable.title: Portable mode
docs.preview.mac: On macOS, Quick Look also offers to open a file in the system's own Quick Look, for formats the system can show and Sourcerer cannot.
docs.preview.pane: View → Preview (Alt+P) shows the selected file beside the results: pictures, text and code, and documents.
docs.preview.play: Audio and video play in the pane, with play and pause, seeking, looping and volume. Audio draws a waveform you can click, with its codec, sample rate, channels and loudness beneath it.
docs.preview.quickLook: <kbd>Space</kbd> opens Quick Look, a large preview over the window. The arrow keys keep moving through the results while it is open, and <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes it.
docs.preview.title: Preview and Quick Look
docs.privacy.mode: Privacy Mode stops recording recent searches and switches off the property lens, which reads inside files.
docs.privacy.reports.page: Report opens the report page, freallyproducts.com/freally-sourcerer/report/, in your browser, with the technical facts already filled in: you can read them but not change them. You add what you were doing and, if you like, an email address.
docs.privacy.reports.send: Nothing is sent unless you press Send on that page, and nothing is ever sent in the background.
docs.privacy.reports.title: Reporting a problem
docs.privacy.reports.where: When the app runs into an error, its message has a Report button beside it. After a crash, the next launch offers Report or Dismiss.
docs.privacy.telemetry: There is no telemetry. The index is built and kept on your own computer, and nothing about your files or your searches is sent anywhere.
docs.privacy.title: Privacy and the network
docs.privacy.updates: The app asks whether a newer version exists once a day; in Settings → Privacy & Updates you can make that weekly, monthly or never, or check now. It asks before installing anything, naming both versions, and a portable copy never checks.
docs.rename.case: Change the case, and choose whether the rule applies to the name alone or to the extension too. By default extensions are left alone.
docs.rename.check: Rows that would collide, overwrite a file or make a name the system refuses are marked, and nothing is renamed while any row is marked: the batch happens whole or not at all.
docs.rename.find: Find and replace, as plain text or as a regular expression, with $1, $2 for what it captured.
docs.rename.intro: Select the results to rename and press <kbd>F2</kbd>. You describe the change once, and every old and new name is shown before anything touches the disk.
docs.rename.number: {n} in the replacement numbers the files in the order of the preview; {n:03} pads the number to three digits.
docs.rename.title: Renaming in bulk
docs.rename.undo: <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> undoes a rename, even after you restart the app, and <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+Z</kbd> redoes it. On Windows and Linux, Undo also brings a deleted file back from the Recycle Bin or the Trash. On macOS it cannot: restore the file from the Trash yourself.
docs.results.commands: Commands of your own, from Settings → General → Custom Commands, with {path}, {dir}, {name}, {stem} and {ext} in their arguments. Each runs as a program with arguments, never as a shell line, and the app asks once before a program runs for the first time.
docs.results.copy: Copy contents for a text file's body, Copy as file to paste the file itself into a folder, and Copy path list — one per line, quoted, space-separated or shell-escaped.
docs.results.delete: Delete sends a file to the Trash or the Recycle Bin.
docs.results.hits: View hits in context shows every match in a document; <kbd>F3</kbd> and <kbd>Shift+F3</kbd> step through them.
docs.results.intro: Every row is a real file on your disk. Right-click a row for what you can do with it:
docs.results.open: Open, Reveal in file manager, and Open with, which lists the apps your system has registered for that kind of file.
docs.results.terminal: Open terminal here opens a terminal in the file's folder.
docs.results.title: Working with results
docs.results.view: Drag a row into another app as if from your file manager. Click a column header to sort, or use Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9; the + at the end of the header row adds a property as a column. The View menu switches between details and thumbnails. Click the result count in the status bar for statistics on the whole result set: sizes and counts by type, the largest, oldest and newest files.
docs.search.bold: What you typed is shown in bold in the names and paths. A modifier such as ext:json narrows the list rather than being something you look for, so it is not marked.
docs.search.move: Move through the results with the arrow keys, and press Enter or double-click a row to open the file with its usual app.
docs.search.title: Searching
docs.search.type: Type in the search bar. Results appear as you type, grouped by lens, each group with how long it took. Every character narrows them; there is nothing to submit.
docs.search.within: <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+F</kbd> searches within the results you already have. Each term becomes a chip you can remove on its own, so you can step back without retyping.
docs.settings.hotkey: A global hotkey brings the app forward from anywhere, with the search bar ready. Set it in Settings → General → Keyboard. A link of the form freally://search?q=… opens the app with that search.
docs.settings.open: Tools → Options… (Ctrl+,) opens Settings, laid out like Everything's Options: a tree of panels on the left, a box above it that filters panels and options as you type, and OK, Cancel and Apply.
docs.settings.panels: The panels cover the look of the app, search behaviour, results, keyboard shortcuts, the folders, drives and exclusions that make up the index, each lens, privacy and updates, logs, backup and reset, and the language.
docs.settings.title: Settings and the hotkey
docs.start.id: The app's id is com.freallyproducts.sourcerer, and your settings, bookmarks and index are kept in your system's app-data folder under that name. Versions up to 0.23.2 used io.mikeweaver.freally; a newer version moves that folder to the new name the first time it starts, so nothing is indexed again.
docs.start.p1: Sourcerer runs as two parts: a background indexer, freally-indexd, that keeps the index current, and the app you search from. The installer sets up both, and the indexer starts when you sign in.
docs.start.p2: The first time the app opens, a short setup asks which folders to index, the hotkey that brings the app forward, and your language and theme. You can change all of them later in Settings.
docs.start.p3: Then it builds the index. On Windows it reads the NTFS change journal, which is quick; on macOS and Linux it walks your folders, which takes minutes on a large disk. You can search while it works: results fill in as it goes.
docs.start.p4: There are no downloads before version 1.0.0, and the source code is private.
docs.start.title: Getting started
docs.syntax.boolean: A space or AND means both, | or OR either, ! or NOT neither, and parentheses group: (budget | forecast) !draft.
docs.syntax.cjk: Match CJK Phonetics finds Chinese, Japanese and Korean names by their reading: wenjian finds 文件.
docs.syntax.ignore: Ignore Punctuation lets foobar find foo-bar, and Ignore Whitespace lets myreport find my report. Both are off by default.
docs.syntax.intro: Sourcerer understands voidtools' Everything syntax, and adds modifiers for its other lenses.
docs.syntax.mod.anchors: The name starts with, or ends with, the text
docs.syntax.mod.children: Folders by how many items they hold directly; descendant-count: at any depth
docs.syntax.mod.codec: Audio codec, and sample rate in Hz
docs.syntax.mod.dupe: Files that share a name and a size; name-dupe: and size-dupe: match on one of the two
docs.syntax.mod.empty: Empty files and folders; empty:roots finds the top of each chain of folders that holds no files
docs.syntax.mod.ext: Extension, one or several separated by semicolons
docs.syntax.mod.loudness: Measured loudness in LUFS, and dynamic range in dB
docs.syntax.mod.parent: The file is directly inside that folder
docs.syntax.mod.path: The full path contains the text
docs.syntax.mod.property: Any of the seventy-two properties; property: is the long form
docs.syntax.mod.silence: How much of an audio file is silent, from 0 to 1
docs.syntax.mod.size: Size, with kb, mb and gb, comparisons and ranges
docs.syntax.mod.volume: Files on one drive, by its name, even when it is unplugged
docs.syntax.modesMenu: The Search menu toggles Match Case (Ctrl+I), Match Whole Word (Ctrl+B), Match Path (Ctrl+U) and Match Diacritics (Ctrl+M).
docs.syntax.modifiersIntro: Modifiers narrow results by what is known about a file. Combine as many as you like.
docs.syntax.regex: regex: starts a regular expression: regex:^report-\d+. The syntax is Rust's, so there are no backreferences and no lookaround.
docs.syntax.regexBuilder: Enable Regex (Ctrl+R) treats the whole query as a regular expression. The regular expression builder beside the search bar tests a pattern against the names on screen as you type it, with the engine's own error if it is invalid.
docs.syntax.terms: Plain words match anywhere in the name, and every word must match: report 2024.
docs.syntax.title: The query syntax
docs.syntax.wildcards: * matches any run of characters and ? one character, against the whole name: invoice_202?.pdf.
features.audio.body: Find audio by its measured loudness in LUFS, true peak, silence, dynamic range, length, codec and sample rate — not by tags somebody typed.
features.audio.title: Audio by how it sounds
features.content.body: Full-text search in PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, Markdown, source code in 32 languages, JSON, CSV and YAML, mail, and inside archives without unpacking them.
features.content.title: The text inside files
features.everything.body: Everything's search syntax works here too, and its file lists open and export, so a catalogue of a drive moves between the two.
features.everything.title: At home if you come from Everything
features.filename.body: Substrings, wildcards, regular expressions, AND, OR and NOT, and Everything's own modifiers for size, date, extension and path, answered from the index as you type.
features.filename.title: File names, instantly
features.platforms.body: The same app, query language and index on Windows, macOS and Linux, a command line for scripts, and eighteen languages.
features.platforms.title: One app, three systems
features.properties.body: Seventy-two properties read from file headers: image size and camera, video codec and length, document author and pages, a program's architecture and signature, and more.
features.properties.title: What a file says about itself
features.results.body: Open, reveal, copy, rename a whole set of results with a preview and undo it, find duplicates and empty folders, and run commands of your own.
features.results.title: Act on what you find
features.similar.body: The similarity lens finds names near what you typed — a typo, a version number, a different prefix — and a search that finds nothing offers the closest real name.
features.similar.title: Names that are only close
features.title: What is in it
featuresPage.cards.audio.body: Measured, not tagged: loudness in LUFS, true peak, silence, dynamic range, length, codec, sample rate and channels. Sort by loudness or length, and play a file in the preview without leaving the list.
featuresPage.cards.audio.title: Audio by how it sounds
featuresPage.cards.cli.body: The freally command speaks the same query language, prints JSON, NDJSON, CSV or NUL-separated paths, returns exit codes that mean something, and completes in bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell.
featuresPage.cards.cli.title: A command line for scripts
featuresPage.cards.content.body: Full-text search in PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, plain text and Markdown, source code in 32 languages, JSON, CSV and YAML, mail, and inside zip, 7z and tar archives without unpacking them. A viewer steps through every hit in context.
featuresPage.cards.content.title: The text inside files
featuresPage.cards.everything.body: Everything's search syntax, quick filters and file lists, in and out, plus CSV, plain text, playlists and NDJSON. A strict mode checks that a query uses only what Everything understands.
featuresPage.cards.everything.title: At home if you come from Everything
featuresPage.cards.index.body: One index across your drives, kept current by each system's own change feed — the NTFS change journal on Windows, FSEvents on macOS, inotify and fanotify on Linux — so new, renamed and deleted files show up without a rescan. A drive you unplug stays searchable, and its results say which drive they are on.
featuresPage.cards.index.title: A live index of every disk
featuresPage.cards.languages.body: Menus, settings and every dialog switch language live, and Arabic lays out right to left. The app follows your system's light or dark theme, or keeps the one you choose.
featuresPage.cards.languages.title: Eighteen languages, light or dark
featuresPage.cards.names.body: Substrings, wildcards, regular expressions, AND, OR, NOT and grouping, with Everything's modifiers and spellings for size, date, extension, attributes and path, and seven match modes, from Match Case to Ignore Punctuation and matching Chinese, Japanese and Korean names by their reading.
featuresPage.cards.names.title: File names, the way Everything finds them
featuresPage.cards.portable.body: Run it from a USB stick: the index, settings, bookmarks and logs stay in a Data folder beside the app, and nothing is registered with the computer it is plugged into.
featuresPage.cards.portable.title: Portable, if you want it
featuresPage.cards.properties.body: Seventy-two properties read from file headers and searched like any other modifier: image size and camera data, video codec and duration, document author and page count, a program's architecture and signature, installer versions, shortcut targets, archive contents, fonts, mail headers and database tables. Any of them can be a column.
featuresPage.cards.properties.title: What a file says about itself
featuresPage.cards.rename.body: Rename a whole set of results with find and replace, regular expressions, counters and case changes, previewed first and refused if two names would collide. Undo reverses a rename, even after a restart. Find duplicates and empty folders straight from the index.
featuresPage.cards.rename.title: Rename, undo, tidy up
featuresPage.cards.results.body: Open, reveal, Open with, copy the path, the name, the contents or the file itself, open a terminal there, and run commands you define. Space opens Quick Look, audio and video play in the preview, and the result count opens statistics for the whole set.
featuresPage.cards.results.title: Everything you do with a result
featuresPage.cards.similar.body: The similarity lens finds names near what you typed — a typo, a version number, a different prefix — and a search that finds nothing offers the closest real name as a one-click correction.
featuresPage.cards.similar.title: Names that are only close
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.0 does
featuresPage.coming.downloads: There are no downloads before version 1.0, and none on this page.
featuresPage.coming.intro: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. This page is version 1.0, and Sourcerer is built one version at a time: the versions after 0.23 are still to come. Each one on the road to 1.0 is marked with its state. Two of the five lenses — the text inside files and names that are only close — are built but not yet connected to search. They are on this page because they are in 1.0.
featuresPage.coming.title: What is still coming
featuresPage.compare.asOf: Sourcerer's column is version 1.0, which is not out yet, and its price is today's: Sourcerer is free today, and future versions may be sold. The other products change too; this table is as of 2 October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally Sourcerer 1.0 next to the commercial desktop search tools people use today. Every cell for another product comes from its maker's own pages, checked on 2 October 2026, and prices are US list prices as of October 2026 — except where a maker shows no US price, which the cell says.
featuresPage.compare.row.audio: Finds audio by measured loudness, codec, sample rate or length
featuresPage.compare.row.content: Searches the text inside documents such as PDF and Office files
featuresPage.compare.row.liveIndex: Finds files by name from an index kept current as files change
featuresPage.compare.row.portable: Runs without installing, from a USB stick
featuresPage.compare.row.properties: Searches what a file's header says: image size, camera, author, page count
featuresPage.compare.row.similar: Finds a file from a name that is only close
featuresPage.compare.summary: The short version: only Sourcerer has all of it — all three systems, a live index, the text inside documents, audio by its loudness, what a file's header says, and names that are only close.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Where they win: Everything costs nothing, and its 1.5 beta also finds files by their hash; FileLocator Pro searches Outlook mail files; Copernic also searches Google Drive, Dropbox and OneDrive; and DocFetcher Pro finds words similar to the ones you typed inside documents.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side with the commercial tools
featuresPage.free.body: Everything Sourcerer does today is free, for everyone: no paid tier, no subscription and no trial that runs out.
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.lead: One search bar for every file on Windows, macOS and Linux: names, the text inside documents, audio by how it sounds, what a file's own header says, and names that are only close — from one index that keeps itself current.
featuresPage.limits.firstIndex: On macOS and Linux the first index walks every folder, so on a large disk it takes minutes rather than seconds.
featuresPage.limits.headers: It reads properties from file headers only: it does not decode pictures, play video or render documents to find them, so a property a header does not carry cannot be searched.
featuresPage.limits.portable: A portable copy does not update itself: replace its folder with a newer version.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.0 does not do
featuresPage.numbers.audioTypes: audio file types in the Audio filter
featuresPage.numbers.code: programming languages its content search reads
featuresPage.numbers.intro: Each figure is counted from the app's own code and its record of changes. Nothing is rounded up.
featuresPage.numbers.lenses: ways to search one index: file name, content, audio, properties and similar names
featuresPage.numbers.matchModes: match modes, from Match Case to Ignore Punctuation
featuresPage.numbers.systems: operating systems: Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.version: This page describes Freally Sourcerer version 1.0: everything on it is in 1.0, and nothing planned for after 1.0 is on it.
featuresPage.why.careful.body: A rename is previewed and happens all at once or not at all, a delete goes to the Trash or Recycle Bin, and a command of your own runs as a program with arguments, never as a shell line, after asking you once.
featuresPage.why.careful.title: It is careful with your files
featuresPage.why.everything.body: Everything's syntax, filters and file lists behave as they do there, checked by tests, so the habits of years carry over — to two more operating systems.
featuresPage.why.everything.title: It respects what you already know
featuresPage.why.honest.body: A folder that could not be read looks just like an empty one, so Sourcerer names the folders it skipped and why. A count that reached its limit is shown as a minimum, never as an exact number.
featuresPage.why.honest.title: It says what it cannot see
featuresPage.why.journal.body: Every system already records the changes to its files. Sourcerer reads that record rather than walking your folders on a timer, so the index stays current without reading the disk again.
featuresPage.why.journal.title: It listens instead of rescanning
featuresPage.why.lazy.body: A file's properties are read the first time a search asks about it, from its header alone, and kept until the file changes. Nothing decodes a picture or opens a database's rows to answer how wide an image is.
featuresPage.why.lazy.title: It reads only what a question needs
featuresPage.why.local.body: No telemetry. The index lives on your own disk, and nothing about your files or your searches is sent anywhere. The update check only asks whether there is a newer version, and you can switch it off.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is

hero.headline: One search. Every source. Every OS.
hero.sub: Find any file as you type: by its name, the words inside it, how it sounds, what its header says, or a name that is only close to the one you remember.
honest.downloads.body: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. Version 1.0.0 is the first one this site will offer.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads before 1.0.0
honest.firstIndex.body: On Windows, the NTFS change journal lets a whole volume be indexed quickly. macOS and Linux have nothing like it, so the first index there walks every folder: minutes, not seconds, on a large disk. After that, the system's own change events keep it current.
honest.firstIndex.title: The first index takes longer on macOS and Linux
honest.lenses.body: The content lens, which reads the text inside files, and the similarity lens, which finds names that are only close, are built but do not answer searches yet. Today the file-name, audio and property lenses do. Connecting the other two is part of the road to 1.0.
honest.lenses.title: Two of the five lenses are not connected yet
honest.network.body: There is no telemetry, and nothing about your files or your searches is sent anywhere. On its own the app goes online for one thing: to ask whether there is a newer version, once a day unless you change it, and you can switch that off. A bug report is sent only when you choose to send one, after you have seen what it holds.
honest.network.title: What goes online, and what never does
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.unreadable.body: A folder that could not be read looks just like an empty one. Sourcerer lists the folders it had to skip, with the reason and the fix for your system, instead of quietly returning fewer results.
honest.unreadable.title: It tells you what it cannot see
ladder.intro: One line per version. The versions after 0.23 are the plan, in the order they will be built.
ladder.note: A version that is done is built and tagged. It is not a download: there are none, and there will not be until 1.0.0.
ladder.rung.v0.19.84: The first public build: file-name search kept current by each system's own change journal, the query language, the app and its settings, in eighteen languages on Windows, macOS and Linux.
ladder.rung.v0.21.0: Must-have features, part 1 of 3: duplicates, empty folders, Everything's file lists, and every action on a result from its right-click menu.
ladder.rung.v0.22.0: Must-have features, part 2 of 3: the index follows the disk live, Index Health, renaming in bulk with undo, unplugged drives that stay searchable, and a command line for scripts.
ladder.rung.v0.23.0: Must-have features, part 3 of 3, and the stable release: portable mode, audio and video in the preview, Quick Look, a regular-expression builder, and a report of the folders search cannot see. Its fix release, 0.23.2, is the current version.
ladder.rung.v0.24.0: The property lens for images and video: dimensions, camera data, codecs and duration, searchable and shown as columns.
ladder.rung.v0.25.0: The property lens for documents, programs and packages: authors and page counts, architectures and signatures, installers, shortcuts, archives, fonts, mail and databases.
ladder.rung.v0.26.0: Music tags, and more for people who work with audio.
ladder.rung.v0.28.0: Tags, notes and collections for your files.

site.tagline: One search. Every source. Every OS.
what.p1: Every operating system has a search box, and each falls short in its own way. voidtools' Everything made file-name search instant on Windows years ago, and it has stayed on Windows.
what.p2: Freally Sourcerer is that kind of search for Windows, macOS and Linux. It keeps one index of your disks, kept current by each system's own record of file changes — the NTFS change journal on Windows, FSEvents on macOS, inotify and fanotify on Linux — so new and renamed files are found without a rescan.
what.p3: Then it reads further than the name. One query can ask about the name, the text inside a document, an audio file's measured loudness, what an image or a program says about itself in its header, and names that are only close to what you typed.
